officialEvidence.source: Fresh seven NSW Curriculum Year 11 focus-area pages, read 16 November 2026

siteSource.note: No local site checkout exists on this machine; paths are repo paths at this commit.

recommendations: Teach the algebra toolkit (w01 to w06) before function language (w07 to w09), then lines (w10 to w13) and parabola intercepts (w14).
Interval notation is taught in the site's inequality lesson (AT02) but the syllabus places it with domain and range; this route defers it to w09.
w07 needs original two-set (arrow diagram) teaching; the site defines a relation only as ordered pairs.
w14 opens the parabola sequence; vertex form (w15) follows.

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: How do index laws handle negative, zero and fractional powers?

syllabusActions.text: Use index laws to simplify expressions and solve problems involving positive, negative, zero or fractional indices
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Use index laws to simplify expressions and solve problems involving positive, negative, zero or fractional indices

entryKnowledge.text: Positive integer indices, a^m x a^n = a^(m+n) for whole-number powers, square and cube roots.

entries.startBoundary: Recall that an index counts repeated factors of the same base.
entries.stopBoundary: Derive a^0 = 1 and a^(-n) = 1/a^n from the division law, meet a^(1/n) as a root, then simplify and evaluate with mixed indices. Stop before surds (w03) and logarithms (e03).
